A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a novel relation prediction approach that learns to discover and generalize from graph patterns in heterogeneous graphs.

we propose a new method for inductive relation prediction using analogy subgraph embedding learning, and our experiments show its effectiveness on both heterogeneous graph based recommendation and knowledge graph completion.
we present a new method that can be used for relation prediction in graphs and that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods on several datasets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the subgraph patterns in heterogeneous graphs can be used to guide relation prediction, and that such guidance can be achieved by using analogy subgraph embeddings.
we should not ignore the logical patterns that are present in the graph data when designing predictive models.
by explicitly representing logical rules, we can learn more generalizable models for relation prediction.
